passages.note: House Third Reading: Hoffman voted Y on final passage of HB2492, the citizenship-verification registration bill.
Bill status page lists Hoffman as Prime sponsor of HB2492, later signed into law as Chapter 99.

passages.provision_quote: any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship.
passages.note: Enacted text of HB2492 requires satisfactory (documentary) evidence of citizenship to register, with rejection of applications lacking it.

rows.reasoning: Hoffman was the prime sponsor of and voted Y (House Third Reading, 31-26-3-0-0) on HB2492 (2022), whose enacted text requires that 'any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship' and directs rejection of applications lacking it, matching the rung text 'Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote.' He acted on this as a State Representative before becoming a State Senator in the same legislature, so the record is in-term for the current seat.
